quote: If decoherence is “untestable” relative to collapse, then so too, collapse is “untestable” relative to decoherence.
content: This symmetry holds for the informal textbook postulate and fails for every collapse theory that has actually been proposed. Dynamical collapse models predict deviations from unitary quantum mechanics: a mass-dependent loss of interference, spontaneous heating of matter, and, for the Diósi–Penrose gravitational version, X-ray emission from the collapse noise. Those predictions are being tested. Matter-wave interference has been pushed past 25,000 atomic mass units without deviation (Fein et al. (2019)), cantilever experiments bound the CSL parameters (Vinante et al. (2017)), and an underground germanium experiment excluded the natural parameter range of the Diósi–Penrose model (Donadi et al. (2021)). Collapse, in its specified forms, is more testable than Everett, not equally untestable, and the tests are going against it, which is evidence for unitarity the essay could have used. The essay instead chooses as its opponent the one version of collapse that makes no predictions and then argues that testability is symmetric. Against the collapse theories physicists actually work on, the asymmetry runs the other way: they can lose, and Everett, as formulated in this sequence, cannot.

quote: The events surrounding the decoherence controversy may be unique in scientific history, marking the first time that serious scientists have come forward and said that by historical accident humanity has developed a powerful, successful, mathematical physical theory that includes angels.
content: It is not the first time; it is the second most famous case, and the first was Einstein’s. Lorentz’s ether theory of 1904 and special relativity of 1905 make identical predictions for every experiment; Lorentz’s theory contains an undetectable ether frame in which the true simultaneity holds, and Einstein’s removes it as an idle postulate. The removal was argued on grounds of simplicity and of the unnaturalness of a structure that the theory’s own dynamics conspires to hide, which is the essay’s argument about collapse, and it was made by serious scientists about the most successful physics of its day. Newton’s absolute space, which no observation could detect, was another, removed by Mach’s criticism and Einstein’s. The essay’s “angels” are the ether, and the comparison is worth making because it shows what the ether case had that the collapse case does not: an alternative that was fully specified, made all the predictions, and had no unexplained remainder. Relativity did not have to say “and the Lorentz transformations, for reasons we do not know.” Everett has to say that about the Born rule.

quote: Belief in the existence of separated portions of the universal wavefunction is not additional, and it is not supposed to be explaining the price of gold in London; it is just a deductive consequence of the wavefunction’s evolution.
content: What is a deductive consequence of unitary evolution is that the universal state has components that no longer interfere appreciably. That those components are worlds, each containing observers who see definite outcomes, with a structure that makes “which world am I in” a well-posed question, is not a deduction from the Schrödinger equation but an interpretation of it, and the leading Everettian treatment says so at length: Wallace’s The Emergent Multiverse (2012) argues that worlds are emergent quasi-classical patterns in the sense of Dennett’s “Real Patterns,” picked out by decoherence, with no precise number and no sharp boundaries, and that identifying them requires a criterion of pattern-hood that the formalism does not supply. Kent’s contribution to Many Worlds? (2010) argues that without a precise branching structure the theory does not yet say what it predicts. The essay treats “A ⇒ B” as settled with A the dynamics and B the worlds; the Everettians who have done the work treat the arrow as the research programme. This is the difference between decoherence and many-worlds that the sequence’s vocabulary erases.
